image_description: A bassoon standing vertically against a wall in a dimly lit room. The instrument features a dark reddish-brown wooden body with complex silver metal keywork. A curved metal bocal is attached near the top, and the bell points upward. The background includes a white textured wall on the left and dark shadows/cardboard boxes on the right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument spans nearly the full height of the frame, consistent with the ~1.3m length of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The boot joint at the bottom creates the characteristic U-turn, and the bell section rises parallel to the wing joint, pointing upward.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; only the external tube shape can be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct curved metal tube (bocal) protrudes from the top of the wing joint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex silver keywork with rods and pads is clearly visible along the wooden body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell flare is visible at the top right. While not being played, the diagonal orientation of the main body relative to the vertical axis is consistent with playing posture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits a deep reddish-brown hue with specular highlights indicating a polished varnish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork reflects light with a silver/chrome appearance.
The main structural components are clearly turned wood.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the white wall appears slightly smudged or painterly rather than having crisp plaster detail, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
Some of the thin metal rods and keys appear to merge slightly into the wood or each other without clear mechanical separation, typical of AI struggling with fine intricate machinery.
The connection between the bocal and the wing joint is slightly ambiguous, lacking a clear ferrule or cork seal definition.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and rule out similar woodwinds like contrabassoon or oboe.
To verify the physical connectivity of the complex metal key system and ensure no floating parts or fused mechanisms.
To assess overall image coherence, lighting consistency, and detect subtle generative artifacts in the background and wood grain.

focus_areas: Mechanical integrity of the keywork (rods, pads, levers)
Connection points between joints (boot, wing, bell)
Wood grain realism and polish reflections
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'structural_collapse' artifact noted in the keywork. AI often fails to render the precise mechanical separation of bassoon keys. Verify if the topology auditor confirms fused parts. Also, check if the classifier distinguishes this from a contrabassoon (which is larger and has a different bell curve).
